source.title: How polysemantic can one neuron be? Investigating features in TinyStories.

record.tranche_reason: Applies SAE feature-frequency and neuron-alignment analyses to a TinyStories language model, reporting results on the model’s representations.
record.gate_note: The post reports textual summaries of plots but not their underlying numerical values. It does not test toy-model superposition or manipulate feature sparsity or importance.
record.test_reason: Applies pre-trained SAEs to a real 2-layer TinyStories LM. It reports that interpretable sparse features are recovered and that feature directions are spread over many MLP neurons, which bears on V4. The evidence is exploratory and mostly qualitative.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author finds neuron 703 is the main direction for 475 features (over 400). The most interpretable features examined are not mostly aligned with any neuron, while neuron-703-aligned features were harder to interpret. The post closes with open questions: the underlying feature distribution, whether SAE-found distributions are pathological, automating feature labeling, and possible cross-layer universality of feature directions.
record.recipe_differences: This is an observational SAE analysis of a TinyStories model’s feature frequencies and neuron-direction alignments, not a toy-network superposition experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports different neuron-alignment patterns for sparse and non-sparse feature groups; it does not report other controlled setting comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: An SAE trained on layer-1 MLP activations, fed layer-0 activations by a bug, still gave seemingly interpretable top activations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature directions may partly transfer across layers of the same model (directional universality).

record.problems: Evidence is exploratory and limited to one small TinyStories model and its provided SAEs. Many results are qualitative summaries of plots without their numerical values; feature labeling is qualitative, and the reconstruction comparison uses only a few random prompt stories.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity manipulation, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity or importance as the cause of feature sharing.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested. The author only raises whether the feature distribution is pathological.
No comparison of one-dimensional vs multi-dimensional features.
Only one 33M 2-layer model, one MLP layer and two SAEs. No larger or other LLMs.

missing.what: Histogram of kurtosis of feature decoder vectors: bulk shown, with a tail beyond 3000 (Gaussian = 3). The author takes high kurtosis as possibly suggesting a privileged basis.
missing.locator: Distribution of neuron importance, middle panel

missing.what: Conclusion statement that most features examined don't have most direction power in the first 10 neurons, but some do.

record.verdict_notes: An exploratory blog post. Plot values are not given in the text, interpretability judgments are by one author, and there are no uncertainty estimates. The V4 support is weak in strength but direct in kind.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry is tested.
The post counts features whose SAE directions are most aligned with a neuron, but does not test whether limited capacity or feature importance causes sharing or dedicated dimensions.
It does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemantic neurons are evidence for superposition.
Tests one 33M-parameter, 2-layer TinyStories model and its second-layer MLP SAE analysis; it does not establish prevalence across larger or other language models.
SAE reconstruction and feature interpretability are discussed, but completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features are not tested.
The post examines SAE decoder directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Measured the average number of active SAE features per token.

conditions.value: main SAE; also described as one of two provided SAEs

rows.value: On average about 30 features active per token.
rows.note: The post does not identify which of the two named SAEs this main-SAE summary refers to.
rows.check: About 30 active features per token (of 32768) is a property of the SAE's training (L0), not a finding about the model's features. It is a descriptor of the SAE, not a result.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE reconstruction loss with the original model loss.

conditions.value: a few random input prompt stories

rows.measure: Reconstruction loss relative to original loss
rows.value: SAE reconstruction loss was on average greater than the original loss by ~25%.
rows.note: The number of prompt stories is not stated beyond “a few.”
rows.check: Baseline should include the zero-ablation comparator: +25% loss with the SAE vs +115% with the MLP ablated. The SAE captures much, but not all, of the MLP's contribution.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V4. SAE reconstruction increases loss by approximately 25% relative to original loss; zero-ablating the MLP increases loss by 115%. Incomplete behavioral reconstruction does not establish incomplete occurrence of V4's distributed or recoverable sparse features.
source_check.problem: The partial state treats completeness of reconstruction as a requirement of V4.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Measured per-feature activation frequency in tokens.
rows.measure: Feature probability, defined as tokens on which a feature is active divided by total tokens
rows.value: The post describes some features as active almost all the time and many as occurring once every 1000 or 10000 tokens; it says low-sparsity features are approximately power-law distributed, while the more sparse tail can be described by either a power law or exponential falloff, with exponential looking somewhat better.
rows.note: The post does not give separate numerical values for the two SAEs in its textual description.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Compared the concentration of SAE feature-direction power across neuron coordinates.

conditions.value: sparse; active fewer than once every 1000 tokens
the two provided SAEs; individual SAE results not specified

rows.measure: Fraction of feature-vector power in the largest neuron and next 9 largest neurons
rows.value: Sparse and non-sparse distributions mostly occupy the same part of the plotted space; the post says sparse features do not extend as far toward having most power explained by the first one or few neurons.
rows.note: Plot values are not transcribed in the post text.
rows.check: For V4 (features spread across many neurons), the conclusion says most features examined don't have most of their power in the top 10 neurons. That is the version's effect, so state should be observed, not partial. The sparse vs non-sparse difference is a secondary contrast.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Counted the features for which each neuron had the greatest feature-direction power.

conditions.value: SAE features examined in the post

rows.measure: Number of features for which each neuron is the most-aligned neuron
rows.value: Neuron 703 is the most-aligned neuron for 475 features; the post says some are sparse and some are not, in a pretty even distribution.
rows.note: The post says many neurons are primary directions for a small handful of features, while some are primary directions for hundreds.

rows.subject: TinyStories 2L, 33M parameter model
rows.operation_detail: Qualitatively compared interpretability of features selected by activation magnitude and by alignment with neuron 703.

conditions.value: about 100 features with largest activations and 50 most strongly pointing toward neuron 703

rows.measure: Qualitative feature interpretability and neuron-direction alignment
rows.value: The largest-activation features were relatively easy to label, were described as very polysemantic, and did not have much of their activation-space power in neuron 703; features with a significant fraction of their direction power toward neuron 703 were harder to interpret.
rows.note: Qualitative assessment; the post links a notebook containing the examined features.
rows.check: The SAE recovers human-labelable features, such as 'Once upon a time', excitement, action and object features. The interpretable ones are not neuron-aligned. Both match V4, so observed rather than partial. The assessment is qualitative.

source_check.notes: Interpretability judgments are qualitative and cover a selected sample; individual alignment results are not explicitly attributed to each SAE. The author reports an earlier layer-0/layer-1 activation bug without identifying any reported result as affected.

statements.correction: TinyStories 2L-33M, final MLP (layer 1), main SAE, a few random prompt stories: approximately 25% average loss increase with SAE reconstruction; 115% with MLP zero-ablation. These measure reconstruction fidelity, not a failure of V4.
statements.problem: The TinyStories numbers and incomplete-reconstruction interpretation are correct, but the limits_scope classification does not follow for V4, which does not require complete behavioral reconstruction.
